questions.grammar_rule: 'Can' expresses ability
questions.explanation: 'Can' is used to express ability to do something

questions.grammar_rule: 'May' is used for polite permission requests
questions.explanation: 'May I' is formal and polite way to ask for permission

questions.sentence: You ___ wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Must' expresses obligation or necessity (laws, rules)
questions.explanation: 'Must' is used for rules and legal obligations

questions.sentence: You ___ see a doctor about that cough.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Should' is used for advice and recommendations
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice - it's a good idea but not mandatory

questions.sentence: It ___ rain later. Take an umbrella.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Might' expresses possibility (less certain than 'may')
questions.explanation: 'Might' shows that something is possible but not certain

questions.sentence: She can to speak three languages.
questions.grammar_rule: Modal verbs are followed by base form without 'to'
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Modal fe'llardan keyin 'to' siz asosiy fe'l keladi
questions.explanation: After modal verbs (can, must, should), use the base form without 'to'

questions.sentence: I ___ swim when I was five.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Could' is the past form of 'can' for past ability
questions.explanation: 'Could' expresses ability in the past

questions.grammar_rule: 'Should have + past participle' expresses regret or criticism about the past
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Should have + past participle' o'tmish haqida tanqid yoki afsuslanish
questions.explanation: 'Should have done' = it would have been better if you had done it

questions.original_sentence: I must finish this report today.
questions.correct_answer: I have to finish this report today.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Must' and 'have to' both express obligation, but 'have to' is used more in spoken English
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Must' va 'have to' ikkalasi ham majburiyatni ifodalaydi
questions.explanation: 'Have to' can replace 'must' for obligation

questions.sentence: That ___ be John at the door. He has a key.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Can't' expresses impossibility or strong negative deduction
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Can't' imkonsizlik yoki kuchli inkor xulosani ifodalaydi
questions.explanation: 'Can't' shows something is logically impossible

questions.sentence: She ___ be at home. Her lights are on.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Must' expresses logical deduction/certainty
questions.explanation: 'Must' for deductions shows you are almost certain

questions.sentence: You don't must speak loudly in the library.
questions.correct_answer: You mustn't speak loudly in the library.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Must' has its own negative form 'mustn't', not 'don't must'
questions.explanation: Modal verbs don't use 'do/don't' - they have their own negative forms

questions.sentence: You ___ have seen a ghost. They don't exist!
questions.grammar_rule: 'Can't have + past participle' for past impossibility
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Can't have + past participle' o'tmishdagi imkonsizlik uchun
questions.explanation: 'Can't have done' expresses that something was impossible in the past

questions.correct_answer: She might/may have missed the train.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Might/may have + past participle' expresses past possibility
questions.explanation: 'Might/may have done' = perhaps X happened in the past

questions.sentence: You ___ have been more careful with the vase.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Should have + past participle' for criticism/regret about past
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Should have + past participle' o'tmish haqida tanqid/afsus uchun
questions.explanation: 'Should have done' expresses that something was the right thing but wasn't done

questions.sentence: He ___ have been working all night. He looks exhausted.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Must have been + verb-ing' for deduction about past continuous action
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Must have been + verb-ing' o'tmishdagi davomiy harakat haqida xulosa
questions.explanation: 'Must have been doing' = logical deduction about an ongoing past action

questions.sentence: She must to have arrived by now.
questions.correct_answer: She must have arrived by now.
questions.grammar_rule: Modal + have + past participle (no 'to')
questions.explanation: After modals, use bare infinitive: 'must have arrived', not 'must to have'

questions.sentence: You ___ well be right. I'm not sure.
questions.grammar_rule: 'May well' emphasizes that something is quite likely
questions.explanation: 'May well' = it's quite possible/likely

questions.sentence: I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Would rather + subject + past tense' for preferences about others
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Would rather + ega + o'tgan zamon' boshqalar haqida xohish uchun
questions.explanation: 'Would rather you did/didn't' expresses preference about another person's action

questions.instruction: Express logical deduction about the past
questions.original_sentence: I'm sure she received my message.
questions.correct_answer: She must have received my message.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Must have + past participle' for logical certainty about past
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Must have + past participle' o'tmish haqida ishonch uchun
questions.explanation: 'Must have done' = I'm almost certain this happened
